scenes.line1: How do you make code reusable?
scenes.say: How do you make your code reusable, but still keep it type safe?

scenes.label: Generics
scenes.sub: Write code that works for any type, safely.
scenes.say: Generics let you write code that works for any type, without losing type safety.
Constraints limit which types you can use. Without them, any type goes, but you risk missing members. With constraints, you can safely use required methods or properties.
Here's a generic repository. The constraints make sure T implements an entity interface and has a parameterless constructor.

scenes.question: Why use constraints in generics?
scenes.wrong: To allow any type, for flexibility.
scenes.right: To enforce compile-time safety and enable required operations.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap. Constraints aren't about flexibility. They're for compile-time safety and letting you use required operations.
